description: Customer relationship platform and CRM for contact management, deals, sales activity, pipeline management, and related customer data.
self_serve_details: A free CRM account can be created without a credit card and has no expiration. API credentials are account-scoped: creating legacy private apps requires super-admin access; app scopes and rate limits depend on account entitlements and subscription. Public/multi-account applications use OAuth.
api_details: REST APIs cover CRM objects and related records; webhooks are supported. Private-app documentation shows configurable scopes and object-event subscriptions. Some API areas and limits depend on account entitlements; CMS GraphQL is not treated as general CRM API breadth.
mcp_details: HubSpot documents a remote CRM MCP server for secure, scoped read/write access and a separate local Developer MCP server. Remote setup uses the current developer platform and OAuth credentials; accessible objects/tools depend on configured app scopes and server capabilities.
blocker: Account-specific scopes, super-admin setup for private tokens, and plan-dependent features/quotas; public OAuth apps require developer-platform app configuration.
buildability_rationale: Broad documented CRM REST APIs and an official MCP option support a feasible connector, but production access must respect account scopes, permissions, distribution, and subscription entitlements.

description: Sales CRM for managing leads, deals, contacts, sales pipelines, and related sales activity.
self_serve_details: Users can obtain a personal API token from the Pipedrive app when the company permission set enables API use. Public Marketplace integrations use OAuth and registered app credentials; developer sandbox access is requested through the Developer Hub form. The official pages opened do not settle production-plan pricing eligibility.
api_details: The official REST reference lists core entities including deals, leads, persons, organizations, activities, projects, users, and webhooks; the API covers most core product functionality and has official Node.js/PHP client libraries.
mcp_details: No first-party MCP documentation surfaced in the official developer pages opened. Community/third-party MCP references are not evidence of a Pipedrive-owned server; official MCP ownership/status remains unresolved.
blocker: Company admin must enable API permission for internal tokens; public distribution uses OAuth/app registration, and sandbox requires a request.
buildability_rationale: The documented REST API and multiple auth paths cover core CRM records, but user permission, public-app onboarding, sandbox provisioning, and unconfirmed production-plan eligibility shape implementation.

description: Customizable, data-driven CRM with developer APIs and workspace-level record, object, list, and activity management.
self_serve_details: Attio offers a Free plan (up to three seats), and its pricing page lists API/webhook access and MCP across plan tiers. Workspace API keys are scoped and can only be created/managed by a workspace admin; MCP uses user OAuth and the user's workspace permissions.
api_details: Official REST API supports reading/writing workspace data, with endpoint coverage for records, objects, lists, and related activities; webhooks and an App SDK are part of the developer platform. MCP additionally supports broad workspace read/write operations.
mcp_details: Attio's first-party hosted remote MCP endpoint is https://mcp.attio.com/mcp. Official docs describe OAuth login and tools for searching, reading, creating, and updating workspace records, lists, tasks, notes, meetings, and other content; read operations are auto-approved and writes require confirmation.
blocker: A workspace admin must issue API keys; OAuth/MCP operations are limited to the authorizing user's workspace permissions and scopes.
buildability_rationale: Public REST, webhook, and MCP surfaces plus a free plan make a connector feasible, but credentials and data access remain workspace-admin/user-permission scoped.

description: Open-source CRM with managed cloud and self-hosted deployments, custom objects, and extensible data/workflow features.
self_serve_details: Twenty offers self-hosting and a self-serve managed-cloud trial; the official pricing page lists paid Cloud Pro/Organization plans and Enterprise sales, with API, webhooks, and MCP included for the listed Cloud plans. Cloud trial/ongoing plan and self-hosting infrastructure are different access paths.
api_details: Official APIs provide REST and GraphQL CRUD for people, companies, opportunities, and custom objects, plus metadata/schema management; webhooks and batch operations are documented. Rate limit depends on cloud tier.
mcp_details: Twenty's official pricing page states Cloud workspaces include a native MCP server and documents OAuth-connected AI access; the feature matrix lists MCP on Pro and Organization. This is first-party cloud MCP, not an independently tested self-hosted server.
blocker: Cloud access is trial/plan-based and usage quotas vary by plan; self-hosted deployments require operator setup and API credentials.
buildability_rationale: Broad REST/GraphQL APIs, dynamic OAuth, webhooks, and first-party cloud MCP make an integration feasible, with deployment choice and cloud-tier limits as material constraints.

description: Flexible work-management platform for customizable team workspaces, workflows, collaboration, and lead/project tracking.
self_serve_details: Podio's official developer FAQ says API use is available to free and paid accounts without an API fee, and users can sign up/sign in and create API keys in account settings. Base rate limits apply; higher limits require an account add-on, and some programmatic app-token/elevated-trust paths require contacting support.
api_details: The official developer site calls the API programmable access to Podio functionality and documents REST/JSON areas for apps, items, tasks, files, workspaces, users, and webhooks, with multiple client libraries. Base API limits are 250 resource-intensive or 1,000 standard calls/hour per user/key.
mcp_details: No first-party Podio MCP offer was identified in the official developer materials opened; third-party/community references, if any, do not establish ownership. The official MCP status remains unknown rather than a categorical absence claim.
blocker: Base rate limits; elevated throughput and some programmatic app-token or high-trust operations require add-on or support interaction.
buildability_rationale: A self-serve OAuth2 API, broad CRUD surface, SDKs, and webhooks make a connector feasible, but volume limits and support-gated advanced paths constrain scale and unattended setup.

description: Cloud CRM for managing leads, contacts, accounts, deals, and sales workflows, with API and AI-agent tooling.
self_serve_details: Zoho CRM's official API limits include a Free Edition with 5,000 API credits per rolling 24-hour window. Developers register a client in Zoho's API Console, obtain OAuth tokens, and request user permission; quotas, scopes, roles, and edition limits still apply. Zoho CRM also publishes first-party OAuth MCP servers, which consume the same API credits.
api_details: Official V8 API documentation covers records/modules, metadata/customization, users, bulk operations, notifications, COQL, SDKs, and workflow/webhook-related operations. The API is credit-based and edition-dependent.
mcp_details: Zoho CRM provides first-party prebuilt MCP servers for Data Insights, Data Operations, Module Customization, and Workflow & Process Automation. OAuth authentication uses the CRM user's permissions; MCP calls consume the same API credits as normal API calls.
blocker: OAuth/account role permissions and edition-specific API credits/concurrency limits; MCP calls share the same quota.
buildability_rationale: Zoho offers a broad documented API and first-party agent MCP, including a Free Edition quota, but connector throughput and writable operations depend on user scopes, edition, and credits.

description: Sales CRM for leads, contacts, opportunities, calling, email, SMS, sales activity, and pipeline workflows.
self_serve_details: Close offers a 14-day trial without a credit card and paid subscription tiers. API keys are created in account settings; OAuth is available for user-facing/public integrations. MCP supports OAuth 2.0 dynamic client registration and also scoped API-key access.
api_details: Official REST resources include leads, contacts, opportunities, activities, custom fields/objects, workflows, and events; webhooks and event log support synchronization. Close also documents an OpenAPI spec.
mcp_details: Close operates an official remote server at https://mcp.close.com/mcp with Streamable HTTP and OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration. Scopes separately enable read-only, safe read/write, or destructive write/delete tools; API-key headers are also documented.
blocker: A Close account/subscription is required beyond the limited trial; MCP/API write and destructive scopes need explicit authorization.
buildability_rationale: Close offers broad REST and webhook interfaces plus a first-party MCP server with practical OAuth, but account status, role permissions, and write-scope choices are operational constraints.

description: Google Workspace-oriented CRM for contacts, sales leads, opportunities, pipelines, tasks, and client/project work.
self_serve_details: Copper offers a self-serve trial; API keys are generated from the Copper web app by an admin and used with the owner email. OAuth 2.0 is the preferred route for partner integrations, but official OAuth quickstart says the application must be registered and client credentials obtained by contacting Copper. Current API entitlement by plan was not resolved from the opened pricing matrix.
api_details: Copper's official Developer API is a REST/JSON interface for most Copper resources, using API-key headers or OAuth. Detailed resource coverage includes core CRM entities, but this assessment does not infer unlisted APIs or count endpoints; plan entitlement remains unresolved.
mcp_details: No first-party Copper MCP documentation was identified in the official developer or product pages opened. Third-party wrappers surfaced in discovery but do not establish Copper ownership; status remains UNKNOWN rather than a categorical absence claim.
blocker: Account-admin API-key setup, partner contact for OAuth client credentials, and unresolved plan-level API entitlement.
buildability_rationale: A documented REST API and token/OAuth paths support integration, but multi-tenant app registration and which Copper subscription unlocks API use require confirmation before promising an unrestricted connector.

description: Deal and relationship intelligence platform for professional firms, including pipeline, contact, firm, and investment/deal management.
self_serve_details: DealCloud API access is tenant-specific. An organization administrator must enable the API capability for the user's group; the user then enables/copies an API key in their profile. API documentation directs users without admin access to their organization's administrator or DealCloud Customer Success Manager. First-party MCP additionally requires DealCloud with Celeste licensing and admin/user MCP permissions.
api_details: Official REST APIs cover structured data CRUD, schema/metadata, user management, backups, publications/real-time events, and relationship intelligence. Access is site- and permission-scoped; OAuth2 client credentials yield bearer tokens.
mcp_details: DealCloud's first-party default MCP server is available at a tenant-specific URL. It exposes site schema/context to compatible AI clients; usage requires DealCloud with Celeste licensing, administrator server-management permission, and end-user MCP Access.
blocker: Requires a provisioned customer tenant and system-admin/API capability; MCP use additionally requires the Celeste license and MCP permissions.
buildability_rationale: DealCloud has broad REST APIs and an official MCP server, but both are customer-tenant/permission dependent; this is feasible within an authorized client account, not a public self-serve connector test.
